import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.54

by N. S. Chernikov

Does there exist a group of infinite special rank which can be represented as a
product of two subgroups of finite special rank?

Here a group $G$ has finite special (Prüfer, or Mal'cev) rank $r$ if every finitely
generated subgroup of $G$ can be generated by $r$ elements and $r$ is the least such
integer; otherwise $G$ has infinite special rank. A group $G$ is the product of two
subgroups $A$ and $B$ if $G = AB = \{ab : a \in A,\ b \in B\}$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«7.54»

/-- The special (Prüfer) rank of a group $G$, as an element of `ℕ∞`: the supremum, over all
finitely generated subgroups $H$ of $G$, of the minimal number of generators of $H$. It is
finite and equal to $r$ exactly when $r$ is the least integer such that every finitely generated
subgroup of $G$ can be generated by $r$ elements, and it is `⊤` when no such integer exists. -/
noncomputable def specialRank (G : Type*) [Group G] : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨆ (H : Subgroup G) (_ : Group.FG H), (Group.rank H : ℕ∞)

/-- A group has finite special rank if and only if there is an integer $r$ such that every
finitely generated subgroup can be generated by $r$ elements. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem specialRank_ne_top_iff (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    specialRank G ≠ ⊤ ↔ ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ (H : Subgroup G) [Group.FG H], Group.rank H ≤ r := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := ENat.ne_top_iff_exists.mp h
    refine ⟨r, fun H _ => ?_⟩
    have := le_iSup₂ (f := fun (H : Subgroup G) (_ : Group.FG H) => (Group.rank H : ℕ∞)) H ‹_›
    rw [specialRank] at hr
    rw [← hr] at this
    exact_mod_cast this
  · rintro ⟨r, hr⟩
    refine ne_top_of_le_ne_top (ENat.coe_ne_top r) ?_
    exact iSup₂_le fun H _ => by exact_mod_cast hr H

/--
Does there exist a group of infinite special rank which can be represented as a product of
two subgroups of finite special rank?

The group $G$ is the product of the subgroups $A$ and $B$ in the sense that
$G = AB = \{ab : a \in A,\ b \in B\}$; the product need not be direct or semidirect.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.54» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (A B : Subgroup G),
      specialRank G = ⊤ ∧ specialRank A ≠ ⊤ ∧ specialRank B ≠ ⊤ ∧
      (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.54»

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«7.54»

/-- A group has finite special (Prüfer) rank if there is a finite uniform bound on the
number of generators needed for each of its finitely generated subgroups. -/
def HasFiniteSpecialRank (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG →
    ∃ S : Finset G, S.card ≤ r ∧ Subgroup.closure (S : Set G) = H

/--
Does there exist a group of infinite special rank which can be represented as a product of two
subgroups of finite special rank? Here the product is the setwise product: every element of the
group must have the form $ab$ with $a$ in the first subgroup and $b$ in the second.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.54» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (A B : Subgroup G),
      ¬ HasFiniteSpecialRank G ∧ HasFiniteSpecialRank A ∧ HasFiniteSpecialRank B ∧
        (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.54»
modeling_decisions: Finite special (Prüfer) rank is modeled by the existence of a natural number r uniformly bounding the cardinality of a finite generating set for every finitely generated subgroup.
Infinite special rank is modeled as the negation of finite special rank, i.e. no finite uniform generator bound exists.
The product G = AB is modeled as equality of the setwise product `(A : Set G) * (B : Set G)` with `Set.univ`; no normality, directness, or semidirect-product condition is imposed.
Generating sets are finite subsets of the ambient group whose subgroup closure equals the subgroup; closure equality ensures the generators belong to that subgroup.

  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG →
    ∃ S : Finset H, S.card ≤ r ∧ Subgroup.closure (S : Set H) = ⊤

some natural number. -/
def HasFiniteSpecialRank (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℕ, HasSpecialRankAtMost G r

Does there exist a group $G$ of infinite special (Prüfer) rank and subgroups
$A,B \leq G$ of finite special rank such that $G=AB$? Here $G=AB$ means that
every $g \in G$ can be written as $g=ab$ with $a \in A$ and $b \in B$; no

    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (A B : Subgroup G),
      ¬ HasFiniteSpecialRank G ∧
      HasFiniteSpecialRank A ∧ HasFiniteSpecialRank B ∧
      ∀ g : G, ∃ a : A, ∃ b : B, g = a * b := by

/-!
# Conjecture 7.54

by N. S. Chernikov

Does there exist a group of infinite special rank which can be represented as a
product of two subgroups of finite special rank?

A group $G$ has *finite special rank* $r$ (also called Prüfer rank or
Prüfer–Mal'cev rank) if every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ can be generated
by $r$ elements and $r$ is the least such integer. If no such integer exists,
$G$ has *infinite special rank*. A group $G$ is the product of its subgroups
$A$ and $B$ if $G = AB = \{ab : a \in A,\ b \in B\}$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«7.54»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- The special rank (Prüfer rank) of a group `G`, as an element of `ℕ∞`: the supremum, over
all finitely generated subgroups $H$ of $G$, of the minimal number of generators of $H$. Since
the finitely generated subgroups of $G$ are exactly the subgroups $\langle S \rangle$ for finite
$S \subseteq G$, this is the least $r$ such that every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ can be
generated by $r$ elements, or `⊤` if no such $r$ exists (see `specialRank_le_iff`). -/
noncomputable def specialRank (G : Type*) [Group G] : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨆ S : Finset G, (Group.rank (Subgroup.closure (S : Set G)) : ℕ∞)

/-- `specialRank G ≤ r` if and only if every finitely generated subgroup of `G` can be generated
by at most `r` elements. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem specialRank_le_iff {r : ℕ} :
    specialRank G ≤ r ↔
      ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG →
        ∃ S : Finset G, S.card ≤ r ∧ Subgroup.closure (S : Set G) = H := by
  simp only [specialRank, iSup_le_iff, Nat.cast_le]
  constructor
  · rintro h H ⟨S, rfl⟩
    obtain ⟨T, hT, hT'⟩ := Group.rank_spec (Subgroup.closure (S : Set G))
    refine ⟨T.map (Function.Embedding.subtype _), ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [Finset.card_map, hT]
      exact h S
    · rw [Finset.coe_map, Function.Embedding.coe_subtype]
      exact ((Subgroup.closure (S : Set G)).subtype.map_closure _).symm.trans
        (by rw [hT', ← MonoidHom.range_eq_map, Subgroup.range_subtype])
  · intro h S
    obtain ⟨T, hT, hT'⟩ := h (Subgroup.closure (S : Set G)) ⟨S, rfl⟩
    exact (Subgroup.rank_congr hT'.symm).le.trans
      ((Subgroup.rank_closure_finset_le_card T).trans hT)

/-- A trivial group has special rank `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem specialRank_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton G] : specialRank G = 0 := by
  rw [← nonpos_iff_eq_zero, ← Nat.cast_zero, specialRank_le_iff]
  intro H _
  exact ⟨∅, le_rfl, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩

/--
Does there exist a group of infinite special rank which can be represented as a
product of two subgroups of finite special rank?

Here $G$ has infinite special rank if `specialRank G = ⊤`, a subgroup $A$ has finite special
rank if `specialRank A ≠ ⊤`, and $G = AB$ is the (set-theoretic, not necessarily direct) product
$\{ab : a \in A,\ b \in B\}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.54» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (A B : Subgroup G),
      specialRank G = ⊤ ∧ specialRank A ≠ ⊤ ∧ specialRank B ≠ ⊤ ∧
      (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.54»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.54

by N. S. Chernikov

Does there exist a group of infinite special rank which can be represented as a
product of two subgroups of finite special rank?

Here the special rank (also called the Prüfer rank, or Mal'cev's special rank) of
a group $G$ is the least $r$ such that every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ can
be generated by $r$ elements; $G$ has infinite special rank if no such finite $r$
exists. A group $G$ is the product of two subgroups $A$ and $B$ if $G = AB$, that
is, every element of $G$ is of the form $ab$ with $a \in A$ and $b \in B$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«7.54»

/-- The special rank (Prüfer rank) of a group $G$: the least $r$ such that every
finitely generated subgroup of $G$ can be generated by $r$ elements, or $\infty$
if there is no such $r$. -/
noncomputable def specialRank (G : Type*) [Group G] : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (r : ℕ) (_ : ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → ∃ S : Finset G, S.card ≤ r ∧ Subgroup.closure ↑S = H),
    (r : ℕ∞)

/-- If every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ can be generated by $r$ elements, then the
special rank of $G$ is at most $r$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem specialRank_le {G : Type*} [Group G] {r : ℕ}
    (h : ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → ∃ S : Finset G, S.card ≤ r ∧ Subgroup.closure ↑S = H) :
    specialRank G ≤ r :=
  iInf₂_le r h

/-- A group has infinite special rank if and only if for every $r$ some finitely generated
subgroup cannot be generated by $r$ elements. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem specialRank_eq_top_iff {G : Type*} [Group G] :
    specialRank G = ⊤ ↔
      ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ H : Subgroup G, H.FG ∧ ∀ S : Finset G, S.card ≤ r → Subgroup.closure ↑S ≠ H := by
  simp only [specialRank, iInf_eq_top, ENat.coe_ne_top, imp_false, not_forall, not_exists, not_and]
  exact forall_congr' fun r ↦ exists_congr fun H ↦ by tauto

/--
Does there exist a group of infinite special rank which can be represented as a
product of two subgroups of finite special rank?

Here $G = AB$ is the product of the two subgroups $A$ and $B$ in the sense that every
element of $G$ is of the form $ab$ with $a \in A$ and $b \in B$; the product is not
required to be direct or semidirect.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.54» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (A B : Subgroup G),
      specialRank G = ⊤ ∧ specialRank A ≠ ⊤ ∧ specialRank B ≠ ⊤ ∧
      (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.54»

Special rank of a subgroup A is `specialRank ↥A`, i.e. the special rank of A as a group in its own right; its subgroups correspond to subgroups of G contained in A, so this matches the intended meaning.

by N. S. Chernikov

product of two subgroups of finite special rank?

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«7.54»

/-- The special rank (Prüfer rank, Mal'cev rank) of a group $G$, as an element of
$\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$: the supremum over all finitely generated subgroups
$H$ of $G$ of the minimal number of generators of $H$. It is the least $r$ such
that every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ can be generated by $r$ elements,
and it is $\infty$ if no such $r$ exists. -/
noncomputable def specialRank (G : Type*) [Group G] : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨆ (H : Subgroup G) (_ : Group.FG H), (Group.rank H : ℕ∞)

/-- A group has finite special rank if and only if there is an `r : ℕ` such that
every finitely generated subgroup can be generated by `r` elements. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem specialRank_ne_top_iff (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    specialRank G ≠ ⊤ ↔
      ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ (H : Subgroup G) [Group.FG H], Group.rank H ≤ r := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := ENat.ne_top_iff_exists.mp h
    refine ⟨r, fun H _ => ?_⟩
    have := le_iSup₂ (f := fun (H : Subgroup G) (_ : Group.FG H) => (Group.rank H : ℕ∞))
      H ‹_›
    rw [← specialRank, ← hr] at this
    exact_mod_cast this
  · rintro ⟨r, hr⟩
    refine ne_top_of_le_ne_top (ENat.coe_ne_top r) (iSup₂_le fun H _ => ?_)
    exact_mod_cast hr H

/-- The rank of a finitely generated group is at most its special rank. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem rank_le_specialRank (G : Type*) [Group G] [Group.FG G] :
    (Group.rank G : ℕ∞) ≤ specialRank G := by
  have h : Group.rank G = Group.rank (⊤ : Subgroup G) := Group.rank_congr Subgroup.topEquiv.symm
  rw [h]
  exact le_iSup₂ (f := fun (H : Subgroup G) (_ : Group.FG H) => (Group.rank H : ℕ∞))
    ⊤ inferInstance

/--
Does there exist a group of infinite special rank which can be represented as a
product of two subgroups of finite special rank?

That is, do there exist a group $G$ of infinite special rank and subgroups
$A, B \le G$ of finite special rank with $G = AB$? Here $AB = \{ab : a \in A,\ b \in B\}$
is the set product; $A$ and $B$ need not be normal, and the product need not be
direct or semidirect.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.54» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (A B : Subgroup G),
      specialRank G = ⊤ ∧ specialRank A ≠ ⊤ ∧ specialRank B ≠ ⊤ ∧
      (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.54»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.54

by N. S. Chernikov

Does there exist a group of infinite special rank which can be represented as
a product of two subgroups of finite special rank?

The special (Prüfer) rank of a group is the least bound on the number of
generators needed for each of its finitely generated subgroups.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.54»

/-- A group has finite special (Prüfer) rank if there is a uniform finite bound
on the number of generators needed for each of its finitely generated
subgroups. -/
def HasFiniteSpecialRank (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ H : Subgroup G, Group.FG H →
    ∃ S : Finset H, S.card ≤ r ∧ Subgroup.closure (S : Set H) = ⊤

/--
Does there exist a group $G$ of infinite special rank with subgroups $A$ and
$B$ of finite special rank such that every $g \in G$ can be written as $g=ab$
with $a \in A$ and $b \in B$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.54» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (A B : Subgroup G),
      ¬ HasFiniteSpecialRank G ∧
      HasFiniteSpecialRank A ∧ HasFiniteSpecialRank B ∧
      ∀ g : G, ∃ a : A, ∃ b : B, g = (a : G) * (b : G) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.54»
modeling_decisions: Finite special (Prüfer) rank is modeled as the existence of a natural-number bound r such that every finitely generated subgroup has a finite generating set of cardinality at most r; infinite special rank is the negation of this predicate.
The product G = AB is stated elementwise as every g : G admitting g = a * b with a in A and b in B, without normality, commutation, uniqueness, or direct/semidirect-product assumptions.
Mathlib's Group.FG is used to identify finitely generated subgroups, while generation is expressed by Subgroup.closure of a Finset being top.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's Group.rank gives the minimum generator number only for a group already equipped with Group.FG; Group.FG itself expresses finite generation but neither provides nor uniformly bounds ranks over all subgroups.

new_definitions.why_needed: Mathlib has no predicate for finite special/Prüfer rank, i.e. a uniform finite bound on generator numbers across all finitely generated subgroups.
